  1. net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api

Configuration in your mod

Load your mod’s text colors and animations from its own configuration file. Read that file into TextConfiguration.Settings and call TextConfiguration.apply; repeat the call when your mod reloads its settings.

Initialize text support before creating effects

A dependent Forge mod should declare required-after:chromatic_codes. Chromatic Codes registers the functions that construct its built-in effects during its Forge construction event. The API calls these functions movement factories. Use them from your mod's construction event or later. Keep one installed copy of the library; do not register its renderer mixin again.

Load text settings from your mod’s config file

If your mod already has a file for text settings, use TextConfiguration. Call its useExternalConfiguration() during construction. The standalone listener then skips its file for the rest of this run. The switch leaves the current definitions active; your mod must still read its own file and pass the resulting values to the library.

Read your file and create a TextConfiguration.Settings with the caseSensitive and inlineEnabled flags, followed by the four descriptor lists: colors, effects, namedColors and namedEffects. Pass that record to apply(Settings) on the initial load and each reload. Constructing the record copies the lists; apply validates the descriptors and installs the complete batch.

This API keeps one configuration batch. Each successful apply replaces the previous batch; invalid input leaves it active. The named-case and inline-code flags are shared registry settings. Unrelated registrations remain, but a new entry can replace one with the same kind and exact trigger. Other settings, such as number formatting, can stay in your mod's existing configuration code.

Install a gold code from your mod’s settings

The example uses a fixed list where your config loader would supply its values. Call initialize() during your mod’s construction event after Chromatic Codes, and call reload() after rereading your file.

import java.util.List;
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.config.TextConfiguration;

final class CopperToolsText {
    static void initialize() {
        TextConfiguration.useExternalConfiguration();
        reload();
    }

    static void reload() {
        var settings = new TextConfiguration.Settings(true, true,
                List.of(), List.of(), List.of("[gold]:FFCC00"), List.of());
        TextConfiguration.apply(settings);
    }
}

After this runs, &[gold]Copper tools§r uses the gold color. Calling reload() again replaces the configuration entries from the previous call. Invalid settings throw an exception and leave that previous set active. Other registrations remain unless a new entry uses the same category and exact trigger. The case-matching and inline-code switches apply to the shared text parser.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or settingArgumentsWhat it does
useExternalConfiguration()No argumentsDisable the standalone file listener for this run; existing definitions stay active until your mod replaces them.
Settings(caseSensitive, inlineEnabled, colors, effects, namedColors, namedEffects)Two flags and four descriptor listsChoose name matching and inline-code support, then supply each category of definitions.
apply(settings)Complete Settings recordValidate and install the configuration batch. Invalid input keeps the previous batch.

When you finish: This API retains one configuration batch and replaces it on the next successful apply. It does not return a separate receipt to close. Close any readers opened by your own file loader; use owned registration receipts instead when entries need independent lifetimes.
